title: John Quincy Adams to the Secretary of State, St Petersburg, No. 88, 25 June 1812: the passages Ford printed as not decyphered (NARA M35 reel 3 frames 0206-0207)

documents.shelfmark: NARA M35 reel 3 frame 0206 (triplicate); Ford, Writings of JQA 4:357 '[Nine lines of this paragraph not decyphered.]'

plaintext.source: The clerk's interlinear decode on frame 0206 stops exactly where Ford's gap starts; Ford prints the gap as not decyphered.

transcription.notes: Group transcription in gap88.txt; clear words kept inline. Re-read 22 Sept 2026 from zoomed crops: 168 (not 158), 1426 (not 1425), 302 (not 502); the underlined 1102 at the foot of the left leaf is a catchword (cw:1102), not counted. python measure.py: 133 code groups (docs/_check_profile.py --measure counts 143 tokens including the clear words).

documents.shelfmark: NARA M35 reel 3 frame 0207 (left leaf); Ford 4:358 'remainder of letter ... undecyphered'

plaintext.source: Ford prints the remainder as undecyphered; no decode on the NARA copy recorded in NOTES.

transcription.notes: rem88.txt: 257 code groups, 7 with digits lost in the microfilm gutter (142x, 21x, 15xx, 11xx, 1xxx, 55x, 13xx), counted as unread. python measure.py counts the groups; docs/_check_profile.py --measure counts 298 tokens including the clear line.

system.summary: Numerical syllable-and-word code (the = 1385), about 1,600 numbers; 1-100 mostly whole words; values climb alphabetically only in short runs, then break; superscript o = plural, a mark under a group modifies it.
system.sibling_key: Armstrong's THE=972 code (armstrong/), which Madison's editors said JQA used; tested and ruled out. Pinkney's London code named in Smith's 1809 instructions (Ford 3:327-28) not tested.
system.notes: distinct_symbols = numbers in code_table.tsv (22 Sept 2026: 391 H, 241 C, 311 M, 19 I), built by consolidate.py from pairs_jqa.txt, clerk_*.tsv (interlinear decodes on frames 0048, 0182, 0183, 0184, 0185, 0189, 0190, 0194, 0198, 0206), ford_pairs*.tsv (39 coded 1811 blocks aligned with Ford vol. 4) and slot_inferences.tsv. Homophones: several words have two groups (those 551/651, English 1291/1292, with 1190/1192-era variants, few 329/350). separation is as transcribed; the manuscript uses dots and spaces.

prior_solution.where: Ford printed both No. 88 passages as not decyphered; the clerk's decode on frame 0206 covers only the rest of the despatch. No other reading found. Ford vol. 4 prints the Department's decipherments of OTHER 1811 despatches in the same code; those were used as known plaintext to rebuild the code (22 Sept 2026), not as a reading of No. 88.

conditions.human_role: Project-level: set up Claude Code with Fable 5.1 or Opus 5 and posed the problem with /goal; occasionally offered encouragement or chose which of the model-identified leads to pursue. No target-specific intervention recorded.
tools: align.py (DP alignment of code groups with Ford's printed plaintext)
consolidate.py (merges clerk, Ford and slot sources into code_table.tsv)

solution.what: Checked the Madison editors' claim that JQA used Armstrong's THE=972 code against Ford 3:327-28 and 3:370.
Fetched NARA M35 reels 2 and 3 frames and scored them for code texture (codescore.py).
Applied the 592-entry Armstrong THE=972 table to JQA's 1812 despatches: noise; his code has the = 1385, of = 1576.
Read the clerk's interlinear decodes on frames 0206 and 0189 into pairs_jqa.txt (262 clerk-attested pairs).
Worked out the code's structure: alphabetical blocks of about 50 numbers, shuffled, whole words in 1-100.
Filled groups by slot inference inside the blocks and context (48 I and 93 M pairs).
Ford's nine undecyphered lines (gap88.txt) read 124 of 134 groups: Rumyantsev's strokes at Wilna and the false report of his death.
The remainder on frame 0207 (rem88.txt) renders 212 of 250 complete groups, in threads only.

Located the images of NARA M35 reel 3 in the main checkout (img03, downloaded 18 Sept) and surveyed the contact sheets: interlinear clerk decodes on frames 0048, 0182-0185, 0190, 0194, 0198, 0211 and later; 'decyphered' sheets for 1811 despatches (0011, 0037, 0064, 0067, 0072, 0082, 0092, ...).

Read the clerk's interlinear decodes on frames 0182 (No. 80, 29 Feb 1812) and 0048 (top) by hand, and on 0183R, 0184, 0185, 0190, 0194R, 0198R with two transcription agents: ~2,000 pairs (1,296 H, 869 M) in clerk_*.tsv.

Transcribed 39 coded blocks of 1811 despatches (frames 0005-0132) and aligned them with the plaintext Ford printed from the Department's decipherments (Writings vol. 4) using align.py, checked by eye: 589 C and 270 M pairs in ford_pairs*.tsv.
Merged all sources into one table (consolidate.py, overrides.tsv for 40 disputed numbers): 962 numbers, 391 H, 241 C, 311 M, 19 I. The alphabetical order holds only in short runs.
Re-read the No. 88 groups from zoomed crops of frames 0206 and 0207: three digits corrected (168, 1426, 302) and a catchword (1102) removed; 1081 in the remainder line 5 is blurred.

Alphabetical-slot bracketing of the groups still unread (slots.py): nine grade-I values (168 ey, 1434 journ, 83 opposition, 143 mod, 815 def, 239 sive, 108 comply, 432 net, 726 rate); 1575 and 1540, first slot-inferred as off and along, were then attested by Ford as adv and ambass.

No. 88 re-measured with measure.py and a sense-flag file (sense88.tsv): 379 of 390 groups valued, 355 read as sense (0.910); Ford's nine lines 127/133 (0.955), the remainder 228/257 (0.887). Before this session: 336 of 391 valued (0.859), sense not measured.

outcome.fraction_read_source: python measure.py (22 Sept 2026): 355 of 390 code groups of No. 88 read as sense = 0.910 (gap88 127/133 = 0.955, rem88 228/257 = 0.887, the 7 gutter-cut groups counted unread); groups valued 379/390; without the I-graded values 336/390 = 0.862

outcome.notes: 22 Sept 2026: code rebuilt from eight more clerk-decoded frames and 39 Ford-aligned 1811 blocks; No. 88 re-read and measured for sense. Below the 95% read bar overall (0.910), so read in part; Ford's nine lines alone reach 0.955 counting grade-I values (0.895 without). More interlinear pages remain on reel 3 (0047, 0056-57, 0211, 0228-29, 0233, 0247) and Ford prints the 1812 decipherments; these are the route to the open groups. Model ids: claude-opus-5 (18 Sept), claude-opus-5-5 (22 Sept). outcome.grades counts the 355 No. 88 groups read as sense (gap 101 H 7 C 11 M 8 I; remainder 184 H 17 C 16 M 11 I).
